implementation.principle: smallest safe change, per the campaign's own preferred order -- a new .path unit paired with the EXISTING mrsilent-autonomous-cycle.service; no new .service, no new .timer, no new queue, no new governor, no new proposal store
implementation.proposal.py: Added NEW_PROPOSAL_SIGNAL_PATH (a sibling of PROPOSALS_DIR, contains only a bare ISO timestamp -- no task data/authority) and _touch_new_proposal_signal(), called once at the end of create() only. Failure is caught and ignored (OSError) -- the durable proposal write already succeeded by that point, so a wake-hint failure can never lose work; worst case is the existing timer still catches it.

debugging_note_disclosed_not_hidden: The first two canary attempts genuinely failed to demonstrate event-driven pickup, for two different, now-understood reasons: (1) th3-mcp-http.service was still running the pre-patch in-memory code (forgot to restart it after editing proposal.py) -- fixed by restarting the service; (2) the second attempt's sentinel touch happened to land while mrsilent-autonomous-cycle.service was still busy finishing a concurrent run triggered moments earlier during manual testing, and that specific event did not produce an observable new run before the check. A clean, isolated test (service confirmed idle immediately beforehand) showed the path mechanism itself fires reliably and fast (same-second) once these two testing artifacts were controlled for. The certified canary below was run with the service confirmed idle immediately before submission.
